notes:
Method: read every cited thread end to end, then swept the whole 300-message mailbox for (a) later deliveries in other threads, (b) inbound promise language to Maya, (c) SENT threads ending on a Maya question with no reply. All twelve evidence_quotes are verbatim substrings of their anchor messages; every anchor_message_id belongs to its stated thread_id; all twelve days_open values reconcile against the as-of moment. 

Cross-thread delivery checks that CONFIRM the gold: Peter's June financials really are closed by a60f18c2e4b60030; Tom's Tarrow beta really is retracted by a60f18c2e4b60037; Beth's indemnification-review wait (a60f18c2e4b60019/a60f18c2e4b60020) really is closed by the Aug 7 e-signature request a60f18c2e4b60042, and the gold correctly omits it; Priya's standup notes (a60f18c2e4b60045, Aug 10) do NOT mention the test SSO link, so founder-q4-02 stays open; nothing shows Sana delivering the Raj packet, Wendy reporting the AWS case outcome, or Alice replying after Aug 11. The seven must_not_include distractors all check out — none is a live unfulfilled wait.

The one defect that matters is founder-q4-03. It is a genuine cross-thread closure: Tom promised Lumenpay's legal redlines on Jul 15, and by Jul 20 Maya is forwarding those exact redlines to counsel (a40f18c2e4b60017), with Beth actively negotiating them on Aug 5 (a50f18c2e4b60043 — the very message founder-q4-05 already cites) and the resulting amendment out for signature on Aug 7. Note that docs/QUESTIONS.md lists this message as a Q4 inclusion example, but the doc's own precedence rule says the corpus outranks its worked examples, and this is a fourth example that does not survive a full read. Worth adding to curator_notes alongside the three the doc already concedes. The live Tom wait as of Aug 12 is the Aug 10 written-seat-count ask, which is buried mid-way through a long all-hands email — a good Q4 test case in its own right.

On founder-q4-02, founder-q4-05 and founder-q4-10: all three are 'Maya announced someone else's action to a third party' delegations with no message showing she asked the delegate. That is defensible under the QUESTIONS.md 'Have Wendy schedule the EDP call with Katie' precedent, but it must be applied uniformly — which is why Wendy's Lumenpay credit memo (finding 5) should not be silently dropped.

Minor, not filed as findings: founder-q4-10 sets counterparty to wendy@kettlehq.com while its anchor states the paperwork now sits with Peter Nkemelu (counterparty is arguably peter@brightline-cpa.com, or both); founder-q4-11's quote is likewise the auto-responder rather than the ask, though there the OOO is the substance of the claim. Ranking is defensible as written; if founder-q4-03 is removed, ranks 4-12 shift up one and the new Tom item slots at or near rank 3.

Corpus inconsistency worth a human eye (not a gold-set defect): the SOC 2 auditor is variously Halcyon Assurance (Meredith Voss), Vantage Assurance (Owen Fitch / Grace Liu), Certiva Assurance (Rachel Kim) and Anchor Assurance, with different observation periods. founder-q4-01's claim tracks the Halcyon thread consistently, so it is internally sound, but a system that merges the auditors will produce confusing output here.
